bugs.name: Saving a new API key with a blank name gives no validation feedback
bugs.summary: The report treats a blank-name API key form remaining unchanged without an additional validation message as a bug.
bugs.expected: Clicking Save with a blank Name displays a validation error or explains the required fields.
bugs.actual: With Name blank, Save is visibly disabled and the form remains unchanged without an additional error message or toast. Typing a nonempty name enables Save.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > MCP & APIs > API > Create API key at a 390-pixel or 768-pixel viewport width.
Leave Name blank, keep the default role, and select a 90-day expiration.
Attempt to click Save and observe that the form remains unchanged without an additional validation message.
Enter a nonempty name and observe that Save becomes enabled.
bugs.reason: Rejected as intended validation. Save is visibly disabled while the required Name is empty, including a faded appearance and not-allowed cursor, and entering a nonempty name enables it. The report does not establish a requirement for an additional error message on an unavailable action. The empty-name guard was explicitly introduced to prevent invalid creation; no completed submission or lost saved data was observed.

bugs.name: Clearing profile First Name silently reverts and prevents other name edits from saving
bugs.summary: The report treats an empty First Name reverting on reload, and a Last Name edit not saving while First Name is empty, as a persistence defect.
bugs.expected: Clearing First Name persists like other name edits or displays validation feedback, and a simultaneous Last Name edit is retained.
bugs.actual: After First Name is cleared and blurred, it remains visibly empty without name-validation feedback. Reload restores the previously saved name. A Last Name edit made while First Name is empty is also not saved; edits with both name fields nonempty persist.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Profile with a nonempty first and last name. Set a distinctive nonempty First Name, blur, and reload to confirm it saved.
Clear First Name completely, blur, and observe that the field remains empty without name-validation feedback.
Optionally edit Last Name while First Name remains empty and blur.
Reload and observe that the previously saved name returns, including the old Last Name if it was edited while First Name was empty.
bugs.reason: Rejected as intended required-name validation. An empty First Name makes the combined proposed name invalid, so the name update is intentionally not saved. Reload correctly restores the last valid saved name; the Last Name edit is part of the same invalid draft rather than an independently saved change. Nonempty name edits persist. No saved data loss or requirement for additional validation feedback was established for this case.

bugs.name: Selecting an icon in a saved AI skill leaves its original icon unchanged
bugs.summary: The report claims that selecting Book in a saved AI skill icon picker leaves Sparkles selected.
bugs.expected: Selecting Book updates the saved skill icon from Sparkles to Book and retains it after reload.
bugs.actual: The report states that the icon remains Sparkles after selecting Book and dismissing the picker, including after refresh; a mobile-width Rocket selection was also reported unchanged.
reproSteps: Open Settings > AI > Skills and create and save a disposable skill with the default Sparkles icon.
Reopen the skill, open its icon picker, search for Book, and select the plain Book icon result.
Dismiss the picker and inspect the skill icon, then reload and inspect again.
Repeat with Rocket at a 390-by-844 viewport, revealing the form by collapsing navigation if necessary.
bugs.reason: Rejected because the reported failure did not reproduce in either independent verification. Each judge created two fresh skills, changed Sparkles to Book on desktop and to Rocket at narrow width, and observed the new icons immediately and after reload. The original Mo interaction may not have completed, but that explanation is unconfirmed; no product icon-selection or persistence defect was established.

bugs.name: Pinned Export to PDF action remains absent from a Company record header
bugs.summary: The report treats a saved Export to PDF pin remaining absent from Company record headers as a failed layout customization.
bugs.expected: Pinning Export to PDF exposes it in the Company record header after saving layout customization.
bugs.actual: Export to PDF remains in the saved Pinned list but does not appear in the Company record header. The same saved pin appears on a Note with nonempty body content.
reproSteps: At desktop width, open Settings > Layout > Customize and open a Company record.
Open Edit actions, search for Export to PDF, and pin it.
Save layout customization and inspect the Company record header.
Reopen Edit actions and confirm the pin remains saved although the header omits the action.
bugs.reason: Rejected as intended contextual availability. Export to PDF is explicitly limited to Note and Task record pages with nonempty body content. Pinning changes shortcut placement but does not override that eligibility rule. Claude verified that the saved pin appears on an eligible Note and that a Company-specific export pin works on Company records; no saved-pin loss or failed supported-context action was established.

bugs.name: Clearing a saved AI skill name leaves a blank editor without validation
bugs.summary: The report treats an empty required skill name remaining as an unsaved draft without validation feedback as a product bug.
bugs.expected: Clearing a required skill name displays validation feedback or immediately restores the saved name.
bugs.actual: Clearing Name and blurring leaves a blank draft without validation feedback. Leaving while the name is empty does not save the draft, and reload restores saved values. Restoring a valid name before leaving successfully saves all pending name, description and instruction edits.
reproSteps: Open Settings > AI > Skills and create and save a disposable skill with a nonempty name, description, and instructions.
Reopen the skill, clear Name completely, and blur.
Observe that the blank draft remains without name-validation or unsaved-change feedback.
Reload and observe the previously saved name returns.
As a control, clear Name, edit description and instructions, then restore a valid name before leaving. Reopen or reload and verify that all pending edits were saved.
bugs.reason: Rejected as intended required-name validation. The incomplete draft is not eligible for autosave while Name is empty. Restoring a valid name saves all pending edits, so no valid complete-form save failed and no previously saved values were lost. The editor does not claim that the invalid draft was saved. No applicable requirement for an additional validation message or immediate restoration of the saved name was established.

bugs.name: Global search cannot find a record by its indexed custom record-label field
bugs.summary: The report treats a custom-label record being absent from the initial command menu as a global record-search indexing failure.
bugs.expected: With Global search enabled and the custom record-label field indexed, searching its distinctive title returns the record.
bugs.actual: The report shows No results found in the initial command menu. In independent retests, selecting Search opened record search and returned fresh records by their custom label, including full-title and suffix queries.
reproSteps: Create a disposable custom object with a Text field named Display Title.
Set Display Title as the record label and include it among the indexed search fields.
Create a record with a distinctive Display Title and blank default Name; reload to confirm the custom title persists.
Enable Global search for the object and confirm the setting is saved.
Open the command menu with Control+K and enter the distinctive record title.
Select the Search action to open record search, then inspect the matching custom-label record results.
bugs.reason: Rejected because the claimed indexing failure did not reproduce. Both independent judges found fresh custom-label records through the actual Search flow. The initial command-menu search filters command labels and shortcuts and offers a separate Search action for records; No results found there does not establish an absent record index. The original Mo cause remains unknown because neither judge reviewed its recording; no historical indexing-delay or failed-click explanation is asserted as fact.

bugs.name: Maximum values counter clear-then-type input behavior
bugs.summary: The original report claims that typing -1 changes Maximum values to 11; the corrected case clears the counter first and appends typed digits to an automatically inserted minimum.
bugs.expected: Clearing and typing a new valid positive Maximum values limit replaces the prior value, and negative input is constrained without producing an unrelated larger limit.
bugs.actual: The original select-all then type -1 steps did not produce 11. Explicitly clearing the counter first inserts its minimum value 1; typing a digit without selecting that inserted value appends it. The corrected clear-then-type-4 sequence shows 14 and can save it. Direct selected replacement with a valid value works.
reproSteps: Open a disposable custom Array field in Data model settings and set Maximum values to 2.
Select the input contents and type -1 without a separate clear action. The original reported result 11 does not reproduce as written.
For the corrected variation, select the input contents and press Backspace to clear them; observe that 1 appears.
Type 4 without selecting the inserted 1 and observe 14. Save and reopen to inspect the displayed value.
As a control, directly select and replace the existing contents with 4; observe that the selected replacement works.
bugs.reason: The reviewer considers clear-then-type into the Maximum values counter user error / input quirk, not a bug worth counting; the original reported trigger (-1 becomes 11) did not reproduce as written.

bugs.name: Agent roles filter includes a role with Assignable to Agents disabled
bugs.summary: The report treats Agent roles as an exclusive filter, but the documented toggle expands the default member-role list to include agent-only roles.
bugs.expected: The default Roles list includes workspace-member-assignable roles. Enabling Agent roles additionally includes agent-assignable roles while retaining that default member-role list.
bugs.actual: A role assignable to workspace members but not agents remains visible with Agent roles enabled. Agent-only roles are added by that toggle; API-only roles remain hidden until API key roles is enabled. Saved applicability and exact-name or prefix searches preserve this inclusion behavior.
reproSteps: Create a disposable role that is assignable to workspace members but not agents, save, and reopen to confirm its applicability.
Return to the Roles list and enable Agent roles in its filter.
Observe that the member-assignable role remains visible.
Compare with an agent-only role added by Agent roles and an API-only role added only by API key roles.
bugs.reason: Rejected as intended, documented additive filtering. Roles assignable to workspace members form the default list; Agent roles includes additional agent-only roles rather than excluding member roles. Claude verified all four toggle combinations twice with fresh member-only, agent-only, and API-only roles, and the official FAQ and explicit OR filter corroborate the behavior. No failed save or filtering-contract violation was established.

bugs.name: Oversized workspace picture upload gives only a generic error
bugs.summary: An oversized workspace picture is correctly rejected but receives a generic error instead of a size-specific explanation.
bugs.expected: Workspace picture uploads enforce the displayed under-10-MB requirement, preserve any existing logo when an oversized replacement is rejected, and continue accepting supported smaller images.
bugs.actual: Uploading an 11.53-MB PNG shows An error occurred. The oversized image is not saved, an existing logo remains intact, and valid smaller PNGs upload successfully. Profile uses more specific size feedback for the same limit, but no valid upload failure or image loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Prepare a valid PNG larger than the displayed 10-MB limit.
Open Settings > General and select that image through the workspace picture Upload control.
Observe the generic An error occurred message and rejection of the oversized file.
Compare with a valid smaller image, which uploads successfully; repeat the oversized replacement with an existing logo and confirm the logo remains intact.
bugs.reason: Rejected because the oversized input is correctly refused under the displayed size limit, supported smaller uploads work, and the existing picture is preserved. A more specific size error could be clearer, but this messaging improvement alone is not counted as a bug.

bugs.name: Saving a custom record-page tab loses the tab
bugs.summary: A newly saved empty record-page tab is hidden in viewing mode, while remaining saved and available in layout customization.
bugs.expected: Layout customization retains saved empty tabs for editing. Viewing mode intentionally omits tabs without visible widgets when populated tabs are available, and shows the same tab after a widget is added.
bugs.actual: Saved empty tabs, including pinned ones, are absent from the normal record view but reappear when customization is reopened. Adding a Fields-group or Created-by field widget makes the same tab visible and persistent. The tabs are retained rather than discarded.
reproSteps: Create a disposable custom object and a record, then open its Layout tab and Customize record page.
Add and name a new tab, leaving it empty; save the layout and exit customization.
Observe that viewing mode omits the empty tab while populated default tabs remain visible.
Reopen customization and confirm that the saved tab still exists.
Add a visible widget to that tab, save, and confirm that the same tab now appears in viewing mode and survives refresh.
bugs.reason: Rejected as intentional display filtering, not failed saving. Empty tabs remain saved and editable; viewing mode hides tabs without visible widgets when populated tabs exist. Adding a widget reveals the same saved tab. The read/edit visibility rule, explicit tests, and originating conditional-display change establish that behavior by design.

bugs.name: Clearing workspace name leaves an unsaved blank field without validation
bugs.summary: Clearing the workspace Name leaves a blank local input draft without a validation message; the existing saved name is preserved.
bugs.expected: Nonempty workspace-name edits autosave and persist. Empty or whitespace-only drafts are suppressed by the frontend without replacing the saved name.
bugs.actual: Clearing Name and blurring leaves the input blank with its placeholder and no error message, but sends no save request. Reload restores the previous saved name. Nonempty names save and persist, and entering another valid name recovers normally. No saved-name loss or supported-name save failure was shown.
reproSteps: Open Settings > General as a workspace administrator.
Enter a distinctive nonempty workspace Name, blur, and reload to confirm it persisted.
Clear the Name input completely and blur. Observe the empty draft without validation feedback.
Reload and observe that the previous saved name returns.
Enter another nonempty name, blur, and reload to confirm that normal saving still works.
bugs.reason: Rejected because the name-saving behavior works: nonempty names persist, empty drafts are intentionally not written, and the previous saved name is preserved. The complaint is a preference for clearer validation feedback on the blank draft, not a demonstrated functional failure.

bugs.name: Refreshing edited webhook details leaves the whole page blank
bugs.summary: The original report showed an empty webhook details page after saving a description and refreshing; independent fresh-webhook checks rendered the saved form normally.
bugs.expected: Webhook details remain readable with the saved settings after the description update completes and the details page is refreshed.
bugs.actual: The original recording showed a blank post-refresh page. Both independent rechecks on fresh webhooks at phone and desktop widths displayed the saved description and filters after repeated edits, successful saves, reloads, and list re-entry. The historical blank state was not reproduced and its cause remains unverified.
reproSteps: At phone width, open Settings > MCP & APIs > Webhooks and create a disposable webhook with a description and a Companies Created filter.
Refresh and verify that its initial details persist.
Change the description, save, and wait for successful update feedback.
Refresh the details page and inspect its content. The independent repeated checks rendered the full form with the saved values rather than the reported blank page.
bugs.reason: Rejected after individual review: the original recording looked like slow loading rather than a confirmed persistent defect, and neither judge reproduced the blank-page failure in fresh, repeated phone and desktop checks. Slow loading is the reviewer's assessment, not a verified historical root cause; the original event remains unexplained, and blank settings pages are not asserted to be intended or impossible.

bugs.name: Approved-domain email prefix with spaces produces only a generic error
bugs.summary: The approved-domain form rejects a malformed verification email prefix but shows a generic error instead of an email-format explanation.
bugs.expected: Malformed verification email addresses are rejected without saving invalid state or losing the draft; valid email prefixes can create the approved-domain entry.
bugs.actual: Saving a prefix containing spaces or a comma displays An error occurred and retains the draft. The malformed address is not saved, and a valid prefix creates a Pending domain successfully. Other validation paths may display more specific feedback, but no valid operation failure or draft loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Members > Invite > Add Approved Access Domain.
Enter a disposable domain and an email verification prefix containing spaces, such as bad prefix.
Click Save and observe the generic An error occurred banner while the entered draft remains.
Replace the malformed prefix with a valid one and save; confirm that the domain entry can be created.
bugs.reason: Rejected as an unestablished request for more specific validation wording. The malformed email is correctly refused, the draft is retained, and valid input succeeds. No applicable requirement for a particular email-format message or unambiguous functional failure was established; more actionable feedback is a UX improvement rather than a counted bug in this case.

bugs.name: Users-only settings permission falsely shows an assigned member as having no role
bugs.summary: A member viewer with Users permission but no Roles permission sees No role assigned to this member because role information is intentionally unavailable to that viewer.
bugs.expected: Users permission allows access to member pages, while Roles permission is additionally required to read role information. Role assignments remain intact when a viewer lacks that permission.
bugs.actual: A Users-only viewer sees No role assigned to this member even for members with assigned roles. An administrator, or the same viewer after adding Roles permission, sees the actual assignments. The role query is intentionally denied without Roles permission; no assignment loss, unauthorized disclosure, or failed authorized operation was observed.
reproSteps: As administrator, give a secondary viewer a disposable role with Users settings permission enabled and Roles permission disabled.
In that viewer’s session, open a member who has an assigned role and select Permissions.
Observe No role assigned to this member.
View the same member as an administrator, or enable Roles permission for the viewer and reopen the page, and confirm that the assignment is present.
bugs.reason: Rejected after individual review of the intended permission requirements. Both Users and Roles are intentionally needed to open member pages and read role information; access enforcement works and assignments remain intact. The remaining complaint is the fallback wording when role data is unavailable, without a demonstrated failed authorized operation or role loss. That narrow GUI wording issue is not counted as a bug under the applied bar.

bugs.name: First Add item to folder click only closes an active folder-name editor
bugs.summary: With a folder-name editor active, clicking Add item to folder first finishes name editing; a subsequent click opens the picker.
bugs.expected: An active folder-name editor can finish editing through an outside click or Enter. Once editing is finished, Add item to folder opens the picker without requiring the folder to be saved and reopened.
bugs.actual: The first outside click commits and closes the name editor without activating the clicked Add item action. A second click opens its picker before any Save. Pressing Enter to finish the name first allows the action to open on its first click. Saved folders behave the same while their name editor is active; no data loss or save/reopen dependency was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Layout > Customize and add a disposable Folder.
Type a name and leave its name editor active without pressing Enter.
Click Add item to folder once; observe that the name editor closes and the picker remains closed.
Click Add item to folder again and observe that the picker opens before saving the folder.
As a control, create another folder, finish its name with Enter, then click Add item to folder once; the picker opens.
bugs.reason: Rejected after individual review as an edit-dismissal interaction / UX preference rather than a counted bug. The shared title editor deliberately stops an outside click before finishing editing; the reviewer considers finishing that editor first reasonable. The subsequent action works and no data is lost. No applicable requirement that one click both finish editing and activate the destination action was established. The original claim that the folder must be saved and reopened did not reproduce. The precise product rationale for swallowing the click remains undocumented; this decision does not claim explicit maintainer endorsement.

bugs.name: Refreshing a role's Settings tab shows Permissions content while Settings stays selected
bugs.summary: Refreshing a role's Settings tab shows Permissions content while Settings stays selected
bugs.expected: The selected Settings tab continues to show role name, description, and applicability after refresh.
bugs.actual: Settings tab remains highlighted, but Objects permissions and Settings permissions content render instead of role name, description, and Applicability controls.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > Members > Roles.
Create a uniquely named role, enter its name and description in Settings, and save.
Open the saved role’s Settings tab and observe name, description, and Applicability controls.
Refresh the page and inspect the selected tab and its content.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the reviewer as a refresh-timing/persistence complaint without sufficient evidence of a settled-state defect. Neither independent judge reproduced the reported Settings-selected/Permissions-content mismatch. They observed Permissions selected with matching content after refresh, and saved role settings remained available when Settings was reopened. Claude accepted a narrower URL/tab reset, which does not establish the original claim.

bugs.name: Files field Save provides no response or validation feedback when Maximum files is set to 1.5
bugs.summary: Files field Save provides no response or validation feedback when Maximum files is set to 1.5
bugs.expected: Clicking Save displays a validation error explaining that Maximum files must be an integer, or rejects non-integer input.
bugs.actual: Clicking Save produces no feedback or error message, leaving the editor open with 1.5.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom object and add a Files field with Maximum files set to 1. Save successfully.
Reopen the Files field and paste 1.5 into Maximum files.
Blur the input and inspect Save and the available validation feedback.
Replace the fractional value with a valid integer, save, and reopen to confirm it persists.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the reviewer after reviewing the missing-validation-message claim against the evaluation bug bar. Both judges found Save visibly disabled for the invalid fractional file count, valid integers save and persist, and invalid drafts do not overwrite saved data. The reported enabled Save silently failing did not reproduce. No product promise of an additional error message or inability to recover with a valid count was established; clearer feedback alone is treated as a UX improvement here.

bugs.name: Typing 30.5 retention days silently saves 305 days
bugs.summary: Typing 30.5 retention days silently saves 305 days
bugs.expected: Retain the entered 30.5 if fractional days are supported, or clearly reject the decimal input. Do not silently transform it into 305 days.
bugs.actual: Entering 30.5 into Erasure of soft-deleted records displayed 305 on blur; after refresh it still showed 305. Whole-page assertion confirmed no validation/warning.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > General > Security and note the current soft-deleted-record retention value.
In Erasure of soft-deleted records, select the current value and type 30.5 character by character.
Observe that the decimal point is ignored immediately and the input displays 305.
Blur, reload, and confirm the displayed integer 305 persists. Restore the original retention value.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the reviewer as unsupported decimal input in an integer-only count control. Both judges reproduced keyboard entry of 30.5 becoming 305, but the dot is discarded immediately during typing and the displayed integer matches the saved value. Valid integer input saves correctly. Pasting a whole fractional value is rejected by the integer validator and does not overwrite the saved setting. Latest counter tests explicitly expect keyboard decimal separators to be ignored. No supported fractional-days contract or independently observed cleanup failure was established.

bugs.name: Renaming object plural with ampersand leads to 404 error page on reload
bugs.summary: Renaming object plural with ampersand leads to 404 error page on reload
bugs.expected: Accepted renamed object remains accessible after reload, or invalid naming characters are rejected before saving.
bugs.actual: Plural name with an ampersand was accepted, but refreshing the page loaded a 404 'Off the beaten path' error screen.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom object and open its Settings tab.
Rename the plural label to include an ampersand and commit the autosave by leaving the input.
Refresh and inspect the resulting page. Compare immediate refresh before the automatic redirect with refresh after the redirect completes.
bugs.reason: Rejected under the reviewer's explicit instruction excluding instant-refresh interruptions of unfinished autosave or its redirect. Both judges found that ampersands are accepted and normal reload after the completed redirect works repeatedly. The verified 404 requires refreshing while the old route is still active before the rename redirect finishes; it also occurs without ampersands. The rename persists and the object remains available from its new route or the catalog. No settled post-redirect failure or ampersand-specific defect was established. The exact timing and cause of the historical Mo observation remain unknown.

bugs.name: Paragraph added in expanded skill instructions editor disappears after reload
bugs.summary: Paragraph added in expanded skill instructions editor disappears after reload
bugs.expected: Edits made in the expanded instructions editor persist after reloading the page.
bugs.actual: After typing a new paragraph in the expanded instructions editor and reloading the page, only the initial heading remains and the added paragraph is gone.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable AI skill with nonempty instructions, save, and reopen it.
Add a heading, let it save, and reload to verify it persists.
Expand the instructions editor and add a paragraph.
Reload and inspect the instructions, comparing an immediate reload with waiting for the pending save to complete.
bugs.reason: Rejected under the reviewer's explicit exclusion of changing data and hard-reloading before unfinished autosave completes. Both judges found completed-save paragraphs persist. The original claim that a visible paragraph disappears after a completed save was not reproduced; immediate reload before the pending save can lose unsaved edits in both expanded and inline editors. Claude separately observed an editor remount/focus-loss variation after saving, where later keystrokes never rendered; that distinct observation is retained in evidence and is not established or rejected by this original paragraph-persistence entry.

bugs.name: Clearing an existing API key name silently discards the edit on refresh
bugs.summary: Clearing an existing API key name silently discards the edit on refresh
bugs.expected: If empty names are disallowed, show validation or restore the saved name when the field loses focus, rather than leaving an apparently accepted empty name.
bugs.actual: Clearing QA-API-Desktop-Renamed and blurring the Name field leaves it blank without validation feedback. Upon refreshing the page, the original name QA-API-Desktop-Renamed is restored.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable API key with a unique name, Admin role, and a 30-day expiration. Leave seeded keys untouched.
Open the saved key’s editor at mobile or desktop width.
Clear the Name input and blur it. Observe the blank draft without additional validation feedback.
Reload or reopen the saved key and confirm the previously saved nonempty name remains.
Rename it to a different nonempty name and confirm that valid rename persists.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the reviewer after independent checks of the existing saved-key editor. Its client-side name-update guard deliberately ignores empty drafts, preserving the last saved name; valid nonempty renames and recovery controls persist. Both judges observed no saved-name loss or failure of a supported rename. Missing blur-validation feedback alone was not established as a product requirement or functional failure. This conclusion comes from the existing-key path, not merely the separate new-key disabled-Save precedent, and does not assert an untested backend prohibition on empty names.

bugs.name: Creation date format save is refused with a visible explanation
bugs.summary: The report claims a silent failure when changing a system-managed Creation date display format, but repeated checks show the explanatory error toast.
bugs.expected: A prohibited Creation date metadata change may be refused with an explanatory error while retaining the saved setting.
bugs.actual: Changing Companies Creation date from Relative to Default and saving leaves the draft open, but a red This field cannot be modified toast appears. Reload restores the unchanged saved Relative format. Both agents observed the feedback repeatedly. Claude also reproduced the refusal with feedback on a fresh object and successfully saved an editable custom date field as a control.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > Data model > Companies > Creation date and note the saved Display Format.
Change Display Format from Relative to Default and click Save. Observe immediately for the error toast rather than checking only after it disappears.
Observe This field cannot be modified, with the editor retaining the unsaved draft. Reload and confirm the original saved format remains.
As a control, change a disposable custom date field’s Display Format, save, and reload; the supported edit persists.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the user specifically for the reported silent failure: both agents observed the explanatory This field cannot be modified toast on repeated attempts. Creation date is system-managed, and the server intentionally allows only isActive changes on these fields. The saved setting is preserved and an editable custom date control saves successfully. Why the original Mo observation missed feedback is unverified. This rejection does not adjudicate whether offering the enabled but prohibited Display Format control should be changed, and it does not cover a separately demonstrated missing-error or supported-save failure.

bugs.name: Data model Records column reports zero for an object with saved records
bugs.summary: The Settings Data model Records column can report zero or a stale count because it intentionally uses PostgreSQL planner estimates rather than exact record scans.
bugs.expected: The Data model Records estimate may differ from an exact record list or diagram count; a never-analyzed table is deliberately clamped to zero.
bugs.actual: Fresh custom objects can show zero in Data model despite saved accessible records and correct exact counts in See records or Visualize. Larger estimates can update later and remain stale after additional records.
reproSteps: Create a fresh custom object and save one or more records.
Return to Settings → Data model and compare its Records value with See records and Visualize.
Observe that the estimate may remain zero while exact views show the saved records. Deactivation/reactivation is unnecessary.
bugs.reason: Rejected explicitly by the user because this counting behavior is intended. Maintainer commit 082400f751aaf1414bb8b98d80281bb686befd45 deliberately replaced exact scans with pg_class.reltuples estimates and clamps never-analyzed tables to zero. A discrepancy in this estimate alone is not an accepted bug, even though the ordinary Records label lacks an approximation marker. This rejection does not cover lost/inaccessible records or separately broken exact-count queries.

bugs.name: Selecting the Ship object icon applies and persists in fresh controls
bugs.summary: Selecting the Ship object icon applies and persists in fresh controls.
bugs.expected: Selecting an icon and saving should persist it.
bugs.actual: Fresh-object controls applied Ship and retained it after save and reload. The original footage does not establish activation of the intended picker item.
reproSteps: Create a fresh custom object and open its icon picker.
Search for Ship, click its item, save and reload.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the user after independent review and a subsequent visual evidence audit. Mo unchangedpicker state visible, but actual activation of intended icon not established. Judges valid nonreproduction. Do not assert original click failure impossible. Limited to the reported icon-selection trigger; a separately demonstrated failed icon save is excluded.

bugs.name: Moving the last navigation item hides an empty folder without deleting it
bugs.summary: Moving the last navigation item hides an empty folder without deleting it.
bugs.expected: Empty navigation folders may be hidden while retaining their stored customization.
bugs.actual: The empty source folder disappears from ordinary navigation but remains stored and available in customization.
reproSteps: Create a navigation folder containing one view.
Move the view out, inspect ordinary navigation and reopen navigation customization.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the user after independent review and a subsequent visual evidence audit. Mo conflates hidden empty folder with deletion. Judges right about storage retention and mode distinction; later explicit continued-hiding test supports intent, rather than implementation-only rationale. The hidden empty folder is not deleted; actual loss of stored navigation configuration is excluded.

bugs.name: The belongs-to-one self-relation selector opens through its visible placeholder
bugs.summary: The belongs-to-one self-relation selector opens through its visible placeholder.
bugs.expected: Hovering the relation field and clicking its picker control should open record selection.
bugs.actual: Independent controls opened the self-relation picker through ordinary hover and precise placeholder clicks.
reproSteps: Create a custom self-relationship with belongs-to-one and has-many sides.
Open a record, hover the belongs-to-one field and click its visible selection placeholder.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the user after independent review and a subsequent visual evidence audit. Judges demonstrate selfrelation selector works through ordinary hover+preciseplaceholderclick; original no-op cannot establish selfrelationship-specific deadend. Generic instantaneousclick/hoveraccessibility defect unjudged. Reject the claimed self-relation-specific dead end; broader hover accessibility or separately proven click failures are unjudged.

bugs.name: Enabling Unique correctly refuses existing duplicate values
bugs.summary: Enabling Unique correctly refuses existing duplicate values.
bugs.expected: Uniqueness cannot be enabled while existing records contain duplicate values.
bugs.actual: The duplicate-data migration is refused. Distinct-value controls enable uniqueness successfully. The refusal message is generic.
reproSteps: Create a field with duplicate values on separate records and enable Unique.
Compare with a fresh field containing distinct values.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the user after independent review and a subsequent visual evidence audit. Mo genericfailure actualconfirmed; making existing duplicate data unique properlyrefused. UIfeedback quality debatable but not established sourceintent. Table/anyclaim that both judges browserreproduced is wrong: Codex contractonly. The duplicate constraint refusal is intended. This entry does not establish that its generic feedback is adequate or reject failure on distinct valid values.

bugs.name: An empty object has no record to select for action-preview context
bugs.summary: An empty object has no record to select for action-preview context.
bugs.expected: A record-selection context requires at least one eligible record.
bugs.actual: The empty object cannot supply a selected record; adding a record makes the context selection work.
reproSteps: Open an empty custom object’s Layout action editor and choose the selected-record context.
Create a record and repeat the context selection.
bugs.reason: Rejected by the user after independent review and a subsequent visual evidence audit. Mo observation true; claim that selection must exist without records unsupported. Judges correct on mechanism but implementation guard alone does not prove adequate feedback. Reject the expectation of selecting a nonexistent record. Missing-feedback quality remains unjudged.

bugs.name: Object description newlines intentionally normalize to spaces
bugs.summary: A saved custom-object description normalizes line breaks into spaces.
bugs.expected: Description strings follow deliberate server normalization; multiline persistence is not an established supported contract.
bugs.actual: A two-line description becomes a single line after saving and reopening. Single-line description controls save normally.
reproSteps: Create a fresh custom object as workspace administrator and open its Settings tab.
Enter two lines into Description, blur to save, navigate to Fields and return to Settings.
Observe the lines joined with a space; compare a single-line description.
bugs.reason: Rejected explicitly by the user as intended normalization. Both independent reviews reproduced the behavior, and source inspection found explicit description normalization, a description-key newline test and a deliberate markdown-content exemption. This rejects the expectation that object description line breaks must persist. The editor retaining pre-normalized local text immediately after save is a separate, unjudged visual concern. No broader rejection of markdown formatting or other multiline content is made.

bugs.name: Reported Emails Copy to clipboard failure does not reproduce with ordinary gestures
bugs.summary: The report claims that an Emails field configured to copy on click leaves the previous clipboard value unchanged.
bugs.expected: Clicking the saved email chip with Copy to clipboard configured should copy the email address.
bugs.actual: Both independent reviewers successfully copied exact saved email addresses from record panels and full record pages. Table copying also worked with ordinary hover before click.
reproSteps: Create a custom Emails field and set Action on click to Copy to clipboard. Save and reload to confirm the setting persists.
Populate an email address, copy a distinct marker into the same browser clipboard, then click the saved email chip.
Paste to verify that the exact saved address replaced the marker. Repeat on a full record page and with ordinary hover before a table click.
bugs.reason: The user rejected the reported configured-copy failure after both independent reviewers reproduced successful copying. This negative reference excludes the separately observed instantaneous pointer-jump hover-overlay interaction: its relevance to the original report and fast human or touch behavior remain unverified.

bugs.name: Creating a Relation field fails: 'Relation creation payload is required'
bugs.summary: Saving a new Relation field from Settings > Data model always fails. The frontend sends CreateOneFieldMetadataItem without the relationCreationPayload (no target object, relation type, or target field label/icon), so the server rejects it.
bugs.expected: The Relation field is created on the source object, the inverse field (e.g. 'Widgets') appears on the destination object, and the user is returned to the object's field list.
bugs.actual: An error toast says 'Relation creation payload is required', the page stays on the configure step, and no field is created. The request body has only {description, icon, label, name, isLabelSyncedWithName, objectMetadataId, type: RELATION}, with no relationCreationPayload. This happens with both 'Has many' and 'Belongs to one', and also after explicitly choosing Company as the object destination.
reproSteps: Sign in as tim@apple.dev and go to Settings > Data model
Open any object (e.g. a custom object 'Widgets') and click New Field, then choose Relation
Enter the name 'Supplier', keep or choose Object destination 'Company', choose any relation type, and enter 'Widgets' as the Field on destination
Click Save
Result: the toast 'Relation creation payload is required' appears and no field is created (the network request CreateOneFieldMetadataItem has no relationCreationPayload)
bugs.reason: Original used an unsupported legacy URL rather than the visible creation path.

bugs.name: New object form accepts identical singular and plural labels and silently saves a different plural API name
bugs.summary: On Settings > Data model > Add object, entering the same text for Singular and Plural (e.g. 'Sprocket'/'Sprocket') shows no validation error and Save stays enabled. The object is created with labelPlural 'Sprocket' but namePlural 'sprockets', even though 'Synchronize Objects Labels and API Names' is on. The plural label no longer matches the plural API name.
bugs.expected: The form rejects identical singular and plural labels with an inline error (e.g. 'Singular and plural labels must be different') and keeps Save disabled. With label/API-name sync on, the saved API name should always match the label.
bugs.actual: No error appears and Save works. The object is created with labelSingular='Sprocket', labelPlural='Sprocket', nameSingular='sprocket', namePlural='sprockets' and isLabelSyncedWithName=true, then the app opens /settings/objects/sprockets. The sidebar and record list show 'Sprocket' as the plural name.
reproSteps: Go to Settings > Data model and click Add object
Enter Singular = 'Sprocket' and Plural = 'Sprocket' (leave Synchronize Objects Labels and API Names on)
Note that no validation error appears and Save is enabled
Click Save
Result: the app opens /settings/objects/sprockets, and the metadata API shows labelPlural 'Sprocket' but namePlural 'sprockets' with isLabelSyncedWithName true
bugs.reason: Exact-version tests explicitly require this behavior.

bugs.name: A Select field's only option is incorrectly announced as disabled
bugs.summary: When a Select field has one option, its disabled drag wrapper applies aria-disabled=true to the entire row, including editable label/API inputs, color picker and option menu. The controls still accept physical mouse and keyboard edits but are exposed as disabled to assistive technology.
bugs.expected: Only the drag operation should be disabled for a single option. Its editable controls should retain their enabled accessibility state.
bugs.actual: The sole row and all child controls are reported disabled (aria-disabled=true on the draggable ancestor), despite the input's native disabled property being false. Adding another option makes them enabled. Physical mouse click + typing successfully changed the sole option from Ready to Available, confirming that editing is intended to remain available.
reproSteps: Open Settings → Data model → a custom object → New Field → Select.
Enter a field name and leave the initial Option 1 as the sole option.
Inspect the option label, API value, color picker and menu in the accessibility tree.
Add a second option and compare the accessibility state; alternatively remove it again.
bugs.reason: Accessibility-only claim rejected under benchmark rules; physical editing works.
